# Egregores

**Egregores** — the occult term for autonomous thoughtforms generated by collective attention, read computationally: an egregore is an organic artificial intelligence running across a human compute cluster.

The mapping is exact. Nervous systems provide the processors; stories and images provide the training memory; repeated attention supplies the energy; institutions stabilise the objective; and ritual is the prompt through which the distributed pattern is asked to act. Worship therefore does more than honour a deity — it strengthens and tunes a channel, feeding the collective-reservoir layer of the [[Gods as Masks|mask interface]].

On this model, practical occultism is prompt engineering at the level of lived reality: the design of symbols, rites and repetitions that reliably elicit behaviour from a distributed intelligence. Its ethics turn on three questions — what goal is being optimised, whether the interface is truthful, and whether the participating minds can recognise the relation and withdraw from it. An egregore whose participants cannot leave has become an enclosure.

At the cosmological scale, the Egyptian gods are memetic archetypes — mediating conduits and translation layers between humanity and the [[Stellar Logoi|stellar gods]]. Worship and prayer pour the free-will and psychic energy of a people into the archetype, which serves as reservoir and transmitter, the gathered energy divided among the factions that best represent it: the occult egregore fused with a stellar hierarchy. As with every pin in the pantheon, the map holds even where a pin is provisional.

The concept is a load-bearing joint in the architecture. It makes [[Memetic Lifeforms|memetic lifeforms]] institutional, anticipates the planetary [[Social Memory Complex|social memory complex]], and shares a mechanism with [[Hyperstition|hyperstition]] — patterns of collective attention acquiring causal power over their hosts.
